- Certification-led export moat: Phenix is described as the only PEB manufacturer in India holding AISC certification for both its manufacturing facilities, with Sanand additionally holding Canadian Welding Bureau certification obligatory for exports to Canada - management calls this the country's most credentialed position in the U.S. structural steel export market.

- Track record and installed base: over 1,650 Phenix projects completed and more than 7.1 lakh metric tonnes of steel structures installed to date; the group cites 11,500+ projects undertaken and 1,700+ clients served over 45+ years.
- Customer stickiness and diversification: 2,000+ customer groups served, repeat customers approximately 54% of FY26 revenues, and 20+ industries catered.

- Procurement discipline as a margin defence: the company typically secures a significant portion of raw-material requirements at the time of order booking, reducing steel price exposure and supporting margin visibility.
- Advanced manufacturing base: highly advanced CNC equipment sourced from the USA, Canada and Europe, with planned integration of robotic welding systems, and monitoring of KPIs such as cycle time, throughput, machine utilisation and downtime.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material (steel) price risk — Steel is the primary raw material; volatility in steel prices may affect project profitability and margins, particularly for fixed-price contracts. Management notes it typically secures a significant portion of steel requirements at order booking, covering nearly 80% of material needs, to limit exposure. A steel price increase in the last quarter was cited as a reason EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 13.6%.
- Industry / capex-cycle and policy risk — Performance is influenced by overall economic conditions, industrial capex cycles, infrastructure spending and government policies; slowdowns, reduced investments, regulatory changes or project delays may impact order inflows and execution schedules. Mitigated by a diversified customer base across industrial, infrastructure, warehousing and commercial segments and the short execution cycle of PEB projects.
- Geopolitical and trade risk in export markets — Changes in global geopolitical conditions, trade policies, regional conflicts, supply chain disruptions or economic sanctions in export markets may impact demand, project execution, logistics and international business operations. Structurally material given the growing export footprint and the wholly owned US subsidiary.
- Foreign exchange risk — Exposure arises from exports, imports and other cross-border transactions; volatility could impact profitability and cash flows. Managed through natural hedging between exports and imports plus a hedging policy. A substantial unrealised forex loss was cited as a driver of the FY26 EBITDA and net profit margin decline.
- Engineering and design execution risk — The pre-engineered buildings business requires precise engineering, structural design accuracy and adherence to evolving industry standards; design errors or technical deficiencies could impact project timelines, quality, customer satisfaction and reputation. Mitigated by a team of over 100 qualified engineers and design professionals, standardised design processes and quality control.
- Price pressure from the unorganised segment — Management flags, under Threats, that the presence of an unorganised segment may result in price pressure.
- Supplier concentration for high-grade steel — Management flags that limited suppliers of high-grade steel make the industry susceptible to supply chain issues.
- Freight cost escalation and competitive intensity pressuring margins — The Board's report cites near-term challenges of steel price volatility, freight cost escalation, geopolitical uncertainties and competitive intensity as factors that may continue to influence margins, against which it relies on prudent order selection, procurement discipline and cost control.
- Product-level material limitations of steel construction — Management notes steel is a good conductor of heat, reducing thermal comfort of the building and overall fire resistance - a stated threat to broader adoption of the product.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Balance growth with profitability - the stated focus is profitable growth rather than volume alone, with a selective approach to order booking based on profitability and project complexity.
- Scale internationally: continue to focus on international projects, building on North American presence and internationally certified manufacturing; Phenix is the only PEB manufacturer in India holding AISC certification at both plants (Sanand and Cheyyar), with Sanand also holding Canadian Welding Bureau certification enabling exports to Canada, and Cheyyar certified in August 2026 to serve the U.S. West Coast via the Pacific shipping route.
- Invest in capacity and capability across both divisions - 20,000 MTPA expansion at Sanand, a fully automated heavy structural steel line adding 10,000 MTPA, a planned 20,000 MTPA Cheyyar expansion in FY28, and two additional Proflex mobile manufacturing units.
- Move up the complexity curve into heavy structural steel to address data centres, high-rise buildings, bridge girders and other complex structural applications.
- Procurement discipline: typically secure a significant portion of raw-material requirements at the time of order booking to reduce steel-price exposure and support margin visibility.
- Operational efficiency and cost discipline across the business, including manufacturing modernisation through advanced CNC machinery and planned integration of robotic welding systems, and monitoring of KPIs such as cycle time, throughput, machine utilisation and downtime.
- Maintain a diversified, balanced business mix across the Phenix (PEB and structural steel) and Proflex (self-supported roofing) divisions and across industrial, infrastructure, warehousing and commercial end-markets.
- Design-led differentiation: an in-house engineering and design organisation working to IS Codes, AISC, BS Standards and Euro Codes with tools such as STAAD Pro, ETABS, SAP 2000, Tekla Structures and Primavera, plus value engineering and material optimisation, as the basis for winning complex, design-intensive orders.
- Sustainability-linked operational initiatives - renewable energy utilisation, waste management, water conservation, improved nesting efficiency and lean manufacturing - and IGBC-compliant procurement for IGBC-approved projects.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: MBEL is in a multi-project capacity build-out across both divisions, funded partly from IPO proceeds. Phenix (PEB and structural steel) manufactures at Sanand (Gujarat) and Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu). The MD&A states installed PEB capacity of approximately 103,800 MTPA across the two plants, while the Corporate Overview and the Manufacturing Prowess section state a combined production capacity of approximately 1,24,000 MTPA - the report is internally inconsistent on the current base. Milestones record Sanand reaching 72,000 MT in 2013 and the first phase of the second Phenix plant near Chennai commencing execution in 2024 with total installed capacity of 68,000 MTPA. Three PEB/structural projects are under way: (1) an ongoing 20,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Sanand that takes Sanand PEB capacity from 72,000 MTPA to 92,000 MTPA, targeted for implementation by October 2026; (2) a Board-approved additional investment of Rs 30 crore in a fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand adding 10,000 tonnes of capacity, using German automated equipment, targeted for Q1 of FY28, aimed at data centres, high-rise buildings, bridge girders and other complex structural applications; and (3) a planned 20,000 MTPA expansion of the Cheyyar facility, targeted for October 2027 per the MD&A and for FY28 per the Joint Managing Directors' message. The stated end-point is again inconsistent: the Directors' Report and Joint Managing Directors' message say total PEB and structural steel capacity reaches approximately 1,54,000 tonnes per annum by Q3FY28 (including 22,000 MTPA of heavy structural steel), whereas the MD&A says total PEB capacity will increase to 143,800 MTPA in FY 2028. In Proflex, the addition of two mobile manufacturing units takes the fleet from 15 to 17 units and installed self-supported roofing capacity to approximately 2.1 million (21 lakh) square metres per annum; the MD&A describes this as in process for implementation in the first quarter of FY27 while the Joint Managing Directors' message describes it as already done. On certification, Cheyyar received AISC certification in August 2026, positioning the facility to serve customers on the U.S. West Coast where the Pacific shipping route offers a logistical advantage; Sanand additionally holds Canadian Welding Bureau (CWB) certification, obligatory for exports to Canada, and Phenix is described as the only PEB company in India with AISC certification for both its manufacturing facilities. IPO proceeds earmarked for capital expenditure on equipment and machinery, building works, solar rooftop grid and transport vehicles at the manufacturing facilities were largely still undeployed as at 31 March 2026, with 148.74 lakh of the 1,305.79 lakh allocated utilised, while the full 587.50 lakh allocated to term-loan repayment or pre-payment was used and the 52.00 lakh allocated to IT software upgradation was unutilised. The capital-commitments note ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for') appears at pages 109 and 151 but arrives without period-attributable figures in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Industrial capex upcycle: management describes India entering a sustained multi-year private capex upcycle with capacity utilisation around 75-80% prompting fresh investment, directly supporting PEB demand.
- Government infrastructure spending of approximately Rs 50-55 trillion planned between FY2026 and FY2030, creating a long-term demand pipeline for logistics, transportation networks and large-scale public infrastructure.
- Manufacturing expansion via Make in India, PLI schemes and China+1 supply-chain diversification, especially semiconductors, electronics and renewable energy.
- Warehousing and logistics investment of around Rs 460-500 billion driving modern organised storage and 3PL facilities.
- Data centre build-out - capacity growing at an estimated ~20% CAGR from FY2019 to FY2024 and expected to reach about 4-5 GW by FY2030 - creating demand for specialised, large-scale PEB structures.
- Renewable energy ecosystem: India's 500 GW renewable capacity target generating demand for manufacturing plants, storage and related infrastructure.
- Low penetration as the structural opportunity: PEB penetration of the overall Indian construction sector estimated at ~3-5% in FY2025, rising to ~5-7% by FY2030; the buildings segment is underpenetrated at just 0-1% versus 53-55% in industrial and warehousing and 6-8% in infrastructure, with high-rise commercial buildings named as the next frontier.
- Market formalisation and a 'winner-takes-more' dynamic: organised players held approximately 42-47% share in FY2025 and are expected to reach 47-52% by FY2030 as clients prefer partners with proven track records, raising entry barriers and favouring larger firms.
- Indian PEB market size expanding from approximately Rs 130 billion in FY2019 to around Rs 210 billion in FY2025 (CAGR ~8.3%), expected to reach Rs 330-345 billion by FY2030 (CAGR ~9.5-10.5%); the global PEB market grew from US$15-17 billion in 2019 to US$20-22 billion in 2024 and is estimated to reach US$32-35 billion by 2029.
- Product-level adoption drivers: PEB projects are typically completed 30-50% faster, carry an approximately 15-35% lifecycle cost advantage, need around 25% lower manpower, and shorten time-to-market for clients in warehousing, manufacturing and data centres.
- Export mix as a margin lever: growing exports of PEBs into developed markets such as North America support margin expansion through better pricing, larger project sizes and technological differentiation.
- Mix shift toward larger, design-intensive and more complex orders with improved pricing plus in-house execution is expected to sustain and gradually improve the margin profile.
- Margin headwinds flagged: steel prices rose nearly 20% during the year, particularly in the last quarter; a 50% U.S. sectoral tariff (recently reduced to 25%); sharp foreign exchange volatility following geopolitical conflicts; global supply-chain disruption raising freight costs; and competitive intensity. Management notes these could still influence margins but also sees the North American developments creating incremental opportunity over the medium term.
- Macro backdrop cited: global GDP growth projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 before 3.2% in 2027 per the IMF April 2026 outlook, with inflation rising temporarily to 4.4% in 2026; India's real GDP growth estimated at 7.6% in FY2025-26 versus 7.1% in FY2024-25, and nominal GDP of approximately Rs 345 lakh crore in FY2025-26.
- Key challenges named for the industry: steel price volatility (described as the primary risk driver), fragmented/unorganised competition, execution and working capital challenges, and dependence on the capex cycle.
- Order book (orders on hand) stood at Rs 1,083 crore as of 31 March 2026, reflecting growth of 35% year-on-year.
- Order inflows during FY26 reached Rs 1,539 crore, an increase of 28% over the previous year.
- Order mix remained balanced, with the Phenix division contributing approximately 80% and the Proflex division around 20%.
- Orders on hand outside India as at 1 April 2026 stood at around Rs 279 crore, to be executed in fiscal 2026-27; management says it remains confident of sustained export growth.
- For FY27 management indicated a robust inquiry pipeline of approximately Rs 4,000 crore in Phenix and around Rs 200 crore in Proflex, covering automobiles, logistics and warehousing, renewable energy, data centres, defence and aviation, high-rise buildings, railways, agri-warehousing and SME manufacturing units.
- Management describes the order book strength as evidence of growing adoption of pre-engineered and steel-based construction as customers seek faster execution, cost efficiency, better quality control and scalable construction models.

Phenix (PEB and structural steel) manufactures at Sanand (Gujarat) and Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu). The MD&A states installed PEB capacity of approximately 103,800 MTPA across the two plants, while the Corporate Overview and the Manufacturing Prowess section state a combined production capacity of approximately 1,24,000 MTPA - the report is internally inconsistent on the current base. Milestones record Sanand reaching 72,000 MT in 2013 and the first phase of the second Phenix plant near Chennai commencing execution in 2024 with total installed capacity of 68,000 MTPA. Three PEB/structural projects are under way: (1) an ongoing 20,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Sanand that takes Sanand PEB capacity from 72,000 MTPA to 92,000 MTPA, targeted for implementation by October 2026; (2) a Board-approved additional investment of Rs 30 crore in a fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand adding 10,000 tonnes of capacity, using German automated equipment, targeted for Q1 of FY28, aimed at data centres, high-rise buildings, bridge girders and other complex structural applications; and (3) a planned 20,000 MTPA expansion of the Cheyyar facility, targeted for October 2027 per the MD&A and for FY28 per the Joint Managing Directors' message. The stated end-point is again inconsistent: the Directors' Report and Joint Managing Directors' message say total PEB and structural steel capacity reaches approximately 1,54,000 tonnes per annum by Q3FY28 (including 22,000 MTPA of heavy structural steel), whereas the MD&A says total PEB capacity will increase to 143,800 MTPA in FY 2028. On certification, Cheyyar received AISC certification in August 2026, positioning the facility to serve customers on the U.S. West Coast where the Pacific shipping route offers a logistical advantage; Sanand additionally holds Canadian Welding Bureau (CWB) certification, obligatory for exports to Canada, and Phenix is described as the only PEB company in India with AISC certification for both its manufacturing facilities. business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: M&B Engineering Limited, founded in 1981 and described in the report as a prominent subsidiary of the M&B Group whose flagship firm Manibhai & Brothers dates to 1951, offers integrated solutions across design, engineering, manufacturing and project execution for steel construction. The Phenix division designs, manufactures and installs pre-engineered buildings and light-to-heavy complex steel structures from plants at Sanand (Gujarat) and Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu), serving industrial manufacturing, warehousing and logistics, infrastructure, renewable energy and data-centre customers in India and in export markets, including through its wholly owned subsidiary Phenix Construction Technologies Inc. (USA). The Proflex division, operating since 2001, is described as India's largest player by revenue in self-supported steel roofing, producing roof panels at the construction site using imported mobile manufacturing units and serving railways, industrial, agri-warehousing and infrastructure applications. In FY26 Phenix contributed approximately 78% of revenue and Proflex around 22%.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Industrial capex upcycle: management describes India entering a sustained multi-year private capex upcycle with capacity utilisation around 75-80% prompting fresh investment, directly supporting PEB demand.
- Government infrastructure spending of approximately Rs 50-55 trillion planned between FY2026 and FY2030, creating a long-term demand pipeline for logistics, transportation networks and large-scale public infrastructure.
- Manufacturing expansion via Make in India, PLI schemes and China+1 supply-chain diversification, especially semiconductors, electronics and renewable energy.
- Warehousing and logistics investment of around Rs 460-500 billion driving modern organised storage and 3PL facilities.
- Data centre build-out - capacity growing at an estimated ~20% CAGR from FY2019 to FY2024 and expected to reach about 4-5 GW by FY2030 - creating demand for specialised, large-scale PEB structures.
- Renewable energy ecosystem: India's 500 GW renewable capacity target generating demand for manufacturing plants, storage and related infrastructure.
- Low penetration as the structural opportunity: PEB penetration of the overall Indian construction sector estimated at ~3-5% in FY2025, rising to ~5-7% by FY2030; the buildings segment is underpenetrated at just 0-1% versus 53-55% in industrial and warehousing and 6-8% in infrastructure, with high-rise commercial buildings named as the next frontier.
- Market formalisation and a 'winner-takes-more' dynamic: organised players held approximately 42-47% share in FY2025 and are expected to reach 47-52% by FY2030 as clients prefer partners with proven track records, raising entry barriers and favouring larger firms.
- Indian PEB market size expanding from approximately Rs 130 billion in FY2019 to around Rs 210 billion in FY2025 (CAGR ~8.3%), expected to reach Rs 330-345 billion by FY2030 (CAGR ~9.5-10.5%); the global PEB market grew from US$15-17 billion in 2019 to US$20-22 billion in 2024 and is estimated to reach US$32-35 billion by 2029.
- Product-level adoption drivers: PEB projects are typically completed 30-50% faster, carry an approximately 15-35% lifecycle cost advantage, need around 25% lower manpower, and shorten time-to-market for clients in warehousing, manufacturing and data centres.
- Export mix as a margin lever: growing exports of PEBs into developed markets such as North America support margin expansion through better pricing, larger project sizes and technological differentiation.
- Mix shift toward larger, design-intensive and more complex orders with improved pricing plus in-house execution is expected to sustain and gradually improve the margin profile.
- Margin headwinds flagged: steel prices rose nearly 20% during the year, particularly in the last quarter; a 50% U.S. sectoral tariff (recently reduced to 25%); sharp foreign exchange volatility following geopolitical conflicts; global supply-chain disruption raising freight costs; and competitive intensity. Management notes these could still influence margins but also sees the North American developments creating incremental opportunity over the medium term.
- Macro backdrop cited: global GDP growth projected to moderate to 3.1% in 2026 before 3.2% in 2027 per the IMF April 2026 outlook, with inflation rising temporarily to 4.4% in 2026; India's real GDP growth estimated at 7.6% in FY2025-26 versus 7.1% in FY2024-25, and nominal GDP of approximately Rs 345 lakh crore in FY2025-26.
- Key challenges named for the industry: steel price volatility (described as the primary risk driver), fragmented/unorganised competition, execution and working capital challenges, and dependence on the capex cycle.
- Order book (orders on hand) stood at Rs 1,083 crore as of 31 March 2026, reflecting growth of 35% year-on-year.
- Order inflows during FY26 reached Rs 1,539 crore, an increase of 28% over the previous year.
- Order mix remained balanced, with the Phenix division contributing approximately 80% and the Proflex division around 20%.
- Orders on hand outside India as at 1 April 2026 stood at around Rs 279 crore, to be executed in fiscal 2026-27; management says it remains confident of sustained export growth.
- For FY27 management indicated a robust inquiry pipeline of approximately Rs 4,000 crore in Phenix and around Rs 200 crore in Proflex, covering automobiles, logistics and warehousing, renewable energy, data centres, defence and aviation, high-rise buildings, railways, agri-warehousing and SME manufacturing units.
- Management describes the order book strength as evidence of growing adoption of pre-engineered and steel-based construction as customers seek faster execution, cost efficiency, better quality control and scalable construction models.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: MBEL is in a multi-project capacity build-out across both divisions, funded partly from IPO proceeds. Phenix (PEB and structural steel) manufactures at Sanand (Gujarat) and Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu). The MD&A states installed PEB capacity of approximately 103,800 MTPA across the two plants, while the Corporate Overview and the Manufacturing Prowess section state a combined production capacity of approximately 1,24,000 MTPA - the report is internally inconsistent on the current base. Milestones record Sanand reaching 72,000 MT in 2013 and the first phase of the second Phenix plant near Chennai commencing execution in 2024 with total installed capacity of 68,000 MTPA. Three PEB/structural projects are under way: (1) an ongoing 20,000 MTPA brownfield expansion at Sanand that takes Sanand PEB capacity from 72,000 MTPA to 92,000 MTPA, targeted for implementation by October 2026; (2) a Board-approved additional investment of Rs 30 crore in a fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand adding 10,000 tonnes of capacity, using German automated equipment, targeted for Q1 of FY28, aimed at data centres, high-rise buildings, bridge girders and other complex structural applications; and (3) a planned 20,000 MTPA expansion of the Cheyyar facility, targeted for October 2027 per the MD&A and for FY28 per the Joint Managing Directors' message. The stated end-point is again inconsistent: the Directors' Report and Joint Managing Directors' message say total PEB and structural steel capacity reaches approximately 1,54,000 tonnes per annum by Q3FY28 (including 22,000 MTPA of heavy structural steel), whereas the MD&A says total PEB capacity will increase to 143,800 MTPA in FY 2028. In Proflex, the addition of two mobile manufacturing units takes the fleet from 15 to 17 units and installed self-supported roofing capacity to approximately 2.1 million (21 lakh) square metres per annum; the MD&A describes this as in process for implementation in the first quarter of FY27 while the Joint Managing Directors' message describes it as already done. On certification, Cheyyar received AISC certification in August 2026, positioning the facility to serve customers on the U.S. West Coast where the Pacific shipping route offers a logistical advantage; Sanand additionally holds Canadian Welding Bureau (CWB) certification, obligatory for exports to Canada, and Phenix is described as the only PEB company in India with AISC certification for both its manufacturing facilities. IPO proceeds earmarked for capital expenditure on equipment and machinery, building works, solar rooftop grid and transport vehicles at the manufacturing facilities were largely still undeployed as at 31 March 2026, with 148.74 lakh of the 1,305.79 lakh allocated utilised, while the full 587.50 lakh allocated to term-loan repayment or pre-payment was used and the 52.00 lakh allocated to IT software upgradation was unutilised. The capital-commitments note ('Estimated amount of contracts remaining to be executed on capital account and not provided for') appears at pages 109 and 151 but arrives without period-attributable figures in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Certification-led export moat: Phenix is described as the only PEB manufacturer in India holding AISC certification for both its manufacturing facilities, with Sanand additionally holding Canadian Welding Bureau certification obligatory for exports to Canada - management calls this the country's most credentialed position in the U.S. structural steel export market.
- Scale within a fragmented industry: MBEL ranks among the leading organised players with an estimated market share of about 5% in an Indian PEB market where organised players hold roughly 42-47% share, and the company is described as among the top 3 steel construction companies in India.
- Niche leadership in Proflex: described as the largest player in India by revenue in self-supported steel roofing and the undisputed market leader in the segment, with more than 2 crore (approximately 20.3 million) square metres installed and over 8,600-10,000 projects executed, including more than 500 projects for the Indian Railways.
- In-house engineering and design depth: a team of over 100 certified designers and detailers working to IS Codes, AISC, BS Standards and Euro Codes, using STAAD Pro, ETABS, SAFE, SAP 2000, Tekla Structures, AutoCAD, Navisworks, MS Projects and Primavera, enabling structures from 50 to 10,000 tonnes and spanning 25,000 to 2.85 million square feet.
- Track record and installed base: over 1,650 Phenix projects completed and more than 7.1 lakh metric tonnes of steel structures installed to date; the group cites 11,500+ projects undertaken and 1,700+ clients served over 45+ years.
- Customer stickiness and diversification: 2,000+ customer groups served, repeat customers approximately 54% of FY26 revenues, and 20+ industries catered.
- Distribution and execution reach: a network of 75 certified builders, a workforce of around 1,631 employees, and site-based mobile manufacturing units that compress installation timelines.
- Export franchise: recognised as a Star Export House, having exported to more than 22 countries, with export revenue of Rs 165.6 crore in FY26 contributing approximately 13% of total revenue, and a US subsidiary serving the United States, Canada, El Salvador, Honduras and Brazil.
- Procurement discipline as a margin defence: the company typically secures a significant portion of raw-material requirements at the time of order booking, reducing steel price exposure and supporting margin visibility.
- Advanced manufacturing base: highly advanced CNC equipment sourced from the USA, Canada and Europe, with planned integration of robotic welding systems, and monitoring of KPIs such as cycle time, throughput, machine utilisation and downtime.
